source.title: Extending BEHRT to UK Biobank: assessing transformer model performance in clinical prediction
source.authors: Yusuf Yildiz; G. Nenadic; M. Jani; David A. Jenkins

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream clinical-prediction metrics across two BEHRT model sizes, a different measurement and setting from language-model pretraining-loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study reports downstream metrics for small and large BEHRT configurations, which bear on V6. Its discussion of neural scaling laws cites prior work and is not a result of this study. The reported MLM metric is APS, not held-out cross-entropy loss, so it does not test V1. No results test loss extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own downstream results for two BEHRT sizes on structured EHR clinical prediction, a new setting. This bears weakly on V6: only two configurations are compared, parameter counts and compute are not stated, and dropout differs between sizes. No loss curves or fits are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that size, terminology and data split affect performance, and that larger models help long-range prediction with marginal short-term gains. They add that smaller models may be practical for near-term tasks, at much lower compute.
record.recipe_differences: This is a BEHRT clinical-prediction model-size comparison, not a language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling sweep; it tests two configurations and reports AUROC and APS rather than fitted power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported size differences vary with prediction task, terminology, data split, and metric.

fits_no_version.finding: On MLM pretraining APS, the large BEHRT model beats the small one in every setting: CALIBER SP1 0.497 vs 0.432, SP2 0.485 vs 0.451, ICD-10 0.353 vs 0.322 (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pretraining-objective accuracy metric, rather than loss, improves with model size for an EHR masked-code model.

record.problems: Only two model configurations are compared; parameter counts and compute budgets are not stated. The authors say the configurations are not exhaustive and that CPRD comparisons rely on published results rather than new experiments. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: None. The MLM APS results were not included because they are not downstream-task results or held-out cross-entropy losses. The table's flattened metric order was interpreted as each task's AUROC followed by APS, consistent with the prose descriptions.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss; MLM is reported only as APS for two sizes.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law form in the EHR modality; only two sizes.
Predictability: no fitted trend, no loss-to-downstream relation, and only two model sizes with unstated parameter counts.

record.verdict_notes: Only two configurations are compared. These differ in width, depth, heads and dropout (0.3/0.4 vs 0.1), so the size effect is confounded with regularisation. There are no parameter counts, seeds or uncertainty. The text says the large model beats the small by <1% 'across all settings' in Tasks 1–3, but r02, r12 and r14 show it lower. The large Task 4 gain for CALIBER SP2 rests on the duplicated 0.634 table cell. The neural scaling laws discussion only cites Kaplan et al. BEHRT on EHR codes is not a text language model, so the V6 link is a loose fit.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out cross-entropy loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run power-law fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or estimates of parameter and token scaling with compute.
The study varies model configurations but does not compare architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No comparison of power-law forms across modalities or training regimes.

Tests only two BEHRT configurations on structured clinical prediction tasks; it does not test downstream language-model benchmarks generally or fit a quantitative predictive relationship between pretraining loss and downstream performance.
No fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation estimates are compared across fitting choices.

relationships.reason: The larger model is better on all Task 4 rows: AUROC +0.016 to +0.233 and APS +0.008 to +0.025 (r07, r08, r15, r16, r23, r24). This shows direction only, from two sizes.
relationships.display_finding: The larger model improved AUROC by 0.016–0.233 and APS by 0.008–0.025 across every tested setting in the two-size comparison.

relationships.condition: Tasks 1–3 (next visit to 12 months), all settings
relationships.reason: Gains are negligible (r01, r03, r05, r06, r09–r11, r13, r17, r19, r21). They are zero in r18, r20 and r22, and APS is lower for the larger model in r02, r12 and r14, so gains from scale depend on the task horizon.
relationships.display_finding: Gains were negligible or zero across next-visit through 12-month prediction settings, with lower average precision for the larger model in some comparisons.
